answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks thus finds them worthless when it returns to them. The delta decay curve is applied at each close, pulse records the drop, and nadir recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 6 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. That bill is paid per identity, so 240 aliases cost 59 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
